No. 1.summary: Charles VI to his envoy at The Hague, Count Windischgrätz: report everything to Pentenriedter, confide in Cadogan; with Alberoni expelled from Spain, France may seek a separate peace with 'the Duc d'Anjou' (Philip V) through Morville; bring the King of Portugal into the Alliance; giving Sardinia to the Duke of Lorraine is 'sehr ideal'; the Emperor insists on the equivalent for Montferrat.
No. 1.en:
Dear Count Windischgrätz. Your letters, which you sent me privately through my Master of the Horse, I have all received
safely one after the other, as you will have learned through him, the Master of the Horse, as also my gracious
satisfaction; but I have not yet answered you particularly, because they consisted partly only of narratives, which I
have had approved for you, and partly you will have received the explanation and orders through the usual chancery
rescripts.

system: The Court Chancellery's two-part nomenclator R5017: numbers 1-400 for letters (with homophones), bigrams, trigrams, nulls and punctuation; 401-977 for words and names in alphabetical order.
